# Independent audit: all-dimensional free-simplex affine neutrality

Source:
`candidate 19aecfceb071d1da`.

Result: PASS, no correction identified. This checks the stated bounded
actual deformation interface and does not promote it to arbitrary mixed
families or arbitrary cap incidences.

## 1. Flux, kernel, and source centroids

The cut face of K intersect H_j has outward normal -u_j, so moving its
flux to the other side of Gauss--Green indeed gives the PLUS sign in(4).
All caps pass through an interior source, hence have positive section
area. Translational neutrality gives theta_j S_j=c rho_j with c>0.
Homothety about y has zero cut-face flux and gives the exact own-volume
identity sum theta_j U_j=beta V.

For arbitrary B, cancellation of its trace term leaves the displayed
matrix equation sum rho_j(g_j-y)u_j^T=0. Applying the one-dimensional
normal kernel to each displacement coordinate forces every g_j-y to be
one common vector. Its membership in every central cut plane, together
with full normal span, makes that vector zero. This argument uses SOURCE
S_j. The application separately distinguishes them from full mixed
coareas defining the original theta; the distinction is correct.

## 2. Weak vertex incidences and coarea normalization

With exactly vertex j strictly captured, the section vertices are the
d intersections of edges v_jv_k with the cut. Fractions t_jk in(0,1]
remain valid even when an excluded vertex is on the plane. These points
are affinely independent, as each has its own positive off-j barycentric
coordinate. Their centroid is y, so t_jk=d y_k.

The affine margins in(11) equal1 at their strictly captured vertices.
The vector r_j=1-d y_j is nonnegative, has sum1, and is a kernel vector
for their gradients. The assumed minimal positive kernel forces every
r_j>0. Thus no weak contact branch is omitted: contacts are ruled out
by a derived identity rather than a general-position assumption.

The pyramid height is1/|grad F_j|. Therefore its source coarea divided
by that gradient norm is dU_j, exactly as in(15). Converting the positive
dependence from raw gradients to unit normals supplies the factor
|grad F_j| and yields theta proportional to r_j/q_j. This verifies every
factor in beta=prod(1-r_j)/(1-sum r_j^2).

## 3. Exact sharp inequality and boundary dimensions

The difference of log partial derivatives has the stated common
positive denominator. Its numerator is
(sum_(k!=i,j)r_k)^2+sum_(k!=i,j)r_k^2, positive for d>=2.
Pair averaging therefore decreases f strictly unless the pair agrees.
Repeated averaging of maximum and minimum coordinates has summable
squared ranges by its exact variance decrement; convergence to the
uniform vector and continuity are justified on the fixed compact
positive coordinate interval. The equality classification follows.

For d=1 the formula is identically1/2 and does not determine y, as
stated. All denominators are positive in the proven open simplex.

## 4. Actual mixed application

The conditional application retains one circuit controlling all deepest
base planes, persistent slack covers elsewhere, regularity, vertex
isolation, and genuine signed affine freedom of the source. Under these
premises both signed upper comparisons force neutrality. The theorem
does not apply its conclusion separately to multiple witness responses
or to supporting-facet allocations. No circular OC input occurs.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
